body:
# Hermóðr, spelled the way the sources wrote it
There is a version of this name the early internet had to settle for: *hermod*. This is the file on how **Hermóðr** replaced it.

Hermóðr has essentially one story, and it is the noblest errand in the Edda: the ride to ransom Baldr, told in Gylfaginning with the plainness of a chronicle and the weight of a funeral. When Baldr fell to the mistletoe dart and the gods' grief had spent itself, Frigg asked who among the Æsir would ride the road to Hel and offer a ransom.  Hermóðr the Bold, called Óðinn's sveinn — his lad, his attendant — stood up.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Hermóðr
- **ASCII form:** hermod
- **Meaning:** "War-spirit"
- **Domain of influence:** Messenger, Courage
- **Pantheon:** Norse
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** ᚼᛁᚱᛘᚢᚦᚱ
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 105 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

Strip **Hermóðr** to *hermod* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **o → ó** — Long ó (ON ó = /oː/): the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Hermóðr** lives at [/sites/hermod/](/sites/hermod/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/hermod/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/hermod/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/hermod/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Hermóðr** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Communication, Messaging & Logistics** — The messenger who rode the nine-night road to Hel and back; the courier run made divine.
- **Defense, Military & Security** — The volunteer for the impossible errand; courage as the mission spec.
- **Travel, Tourism & Place Branding** — The rider of the dark road; the journey there and back as sacred errand.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Norse tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Poetic Edda](/texts/poetic-edda/) and [Prose Edda](/texts/prose-edda/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/hermod/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
